claim: Official MetMalaysia: Northeast Monsoon Nov–Mar brings heavy rain to east coast peninsula, west Sarawak and east Sabah; Southwest Monsoon late May–Sep is drier; inter-monsoon Apr–May and Oct–Nov with afternoon thunderstorms.
quote: the Northeast Monsoon brings heavy rain especially to the states on the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia, west of Sarawak and east of Sabah, while the Southwest Monsoon relatively shows drier weather.

claim: Northeast Monsoon Nov–Mar hits Perhentian/Redang/Tioman, west Sarawak, east Sabah; lowlands 23–33°C with humidity 80%+ year-round.
quote: Northeast Monsoon (November to March) ... Affects: Eastern peninsula (Perhentian, Redang, Tioman islands), west Sarawak, east Sabah ... humidity 80% or more

claim: Perhentian Islands: open Mar–Oct, best May–Sep, peak Jun–Aug, effectively closed Nov–Feb with ferries/accommodation largely unavailable.
quote: Open: March–October; Best: May–September; Peak: June–August; Closed: November–February (monsoon season)

claim: East-coast islands closed Nov–Feb; ferries resume late February; November brings ~25 rain days to Redang/Tioman/Perhentian.
quote: The Perhentian Islands are closed to tourists from November to February due to monsoon season ... 25 rain days in November alone to East Coast islands like Redang, Tioman, and Perhentian.

claim: Most east-coast island accommodation closes during the monsoon due to bad weather and rough seas.
quote: Most accommodation on the Perhentian Islands, along with other east coast islands, will be closed due to bad weather and rough seas.

claim: West coast best Dec–Mar; east coast best Apr–Oct; Borneo best Mar–Oct; regions have opposite wet seasons.
quote: different regions have opposite wet seasons, so you can always find somewhere with good weather

claim: Sandakan (east Sabah) wettest in December (~301mm); Nov–Dec can exceed 400mm; January is mid rainy season.
quote: The wettest period in Sandakan occurs in December, which receives around 301 mm (12 in) of precipitation ... wettest months are usually November and December

claim: Kinabatangan wettest and often flooded Dec–Jan; peak wildlife activity May–Aug when fruiting trees draw animals out.
quote: December and January are the wettest part of the year, as it's often flooded in the Kinabatangan region. Peak wildlife activity tends to occur between May and August

claim: Sabah's wet season runs roughly Oct–Mar; the relatively dry May–Sep is best for wildlife spotting and trekking.
quote: Sabah has its own wet season, which falls roughly from October to March

claim: Kuching (west Sarawak) wettest Nov–Feb during the Northeast Monsoon; January is the wettest month at ~670mm.
quote: pronounced wet season from November to February ... monthly averages of over 400 millimeters

claim: Kuching January is the wettest month with ~672mm of precipitation.
quote: January is the wettest month with 672.3 millimeters

claim: Sarawak is wettest in the Nov–Feb Northeast Monsoon; the drier Mar–Sep window is the better time to visit.
quote: The wettest times are during the Northeast Monsoon months of November to February.

claim: 2026 movable festivals: Chinese New Year 17–18 Feb, Thaipusam 2 Feb, Deepavali 8 Nov.
quote: Chinese New Year 2026 (Year of the Horse) falls on Tuesday 17 February ... Thaipusam in 2026 falls on 2 February ... Deepavali 2026 falls on Sunday 8 November

claim: Ramadan 2026 begins ~20 Feb; Hari Raya Aidilfitri ~20–22 Mar 2026 with a 4-day Raya long weekend and balik-kampung travel surge.
quote: Hari Raya Aidilfitri in Malaysia will be observed on 21–22 March 2026 ... giving a free 4-day Raya long weekend

claim: Transboundary haze from Indonesian peat/forest fires recurs in the Jun–Oct dry season, worst in strong El Niño years (1997, 2015, 2019, 2023).
quote: The high concentration of peat in soil contributes to the haze's density ... peat fires produce the thick and sooty smoke that travels long distances

claim: 2026 haze risk flagged worst since 2015: El Niño ~80% likely by July plus a positive IOD in Jul–Aug, peak haze Aug–Sep, echoing 1997.
quote: El Niño: 80% probability of formation by July 2026 ... Peak Risk Months: August–September ... mirrors 1997 conditions

claim: By late March 2026, rising fire hotspots and scant rain had already raised haze alarm across Southeast Asia.
quote: Fire hot spots and scant rain raise haze alarm in South-East Asia

claim: A Pengerang, Johor peat fire ignited 23 Jan 2026 and grew to ~100 hectares by 27 Jan, forcing evacuations and hitting air quality.
quote: the blaze had spread to 99.54 hectares, roughly the size of 120 football fields

claim: Rainforest World Music Festival 2026 runs 26–28 June at the Sarawak Cultural Village, Kuching.
quote: Rainforest World Music Festival 2026 | June 26–28, Sarawak

claim: West coast best Dec–Mar (escapes NE monsoon); Borneo best Mar–Oct with relatively dry May–Oct for parks.
quote: the best time to visit the West Coast is from December to March ... best time to visit Borneo is from March to October

claim: When the east coast is wet and windy the west coast is nicer and vice versa, so somewhere in Malaysia has good weather year-round.
quote: When the east coast of Malaysia is wet and windy, the west coast is much nicer and vice versa.

claim: West coast best Nov–Mar; east coast best Apr–Oct (hotels close late Oct–Mar); Borneo best Mar–Oct.
quote: Many hotels and restaurants close from late October due to the Northeast Monsoon and reopen around March
